comments.text: Thank you for putting the video together.  I was born and raised in the neighboring county, Luzerne County, during the three decades that this video covered.  Mine fires were ubiquitous in northeast Pennsylvania during those years.  As children, we played among steaming rock outcrops in Laurel Run, another town that had to relocate itself further down the valley to escape a fire in the Red Ash mine.  Until he passed away, my grandfather bootlegged the coal that heated three homes.  We hunted deer and Grouse and black bear in the scrub oak hills and Hemock swamps high above those coal seams.  The Appalachain mountains are really the most amazing place on earth.
